features.name: Mount Sharp
features.subtitle: Aeolis Mons
features.description: The central mound of Gale Crater preserves a layered geological record. Curiosity explores its lower slopes to investigate ancient Martian environments.
features.accuracy: USGS feature center, published to 0.01°. A geographic reference, not a summit or field sampling site.

features.name: Bradbury Landing
features.subtitle: Mars Science Laboratory
features.description: Curiosity’s August 2012 touchdown site on the crater floor. NASA reconstructed the location using descent imagery registered to orbital terrain.
features.accuracy: NASA reports ~5 m relative to terrain with absolute map-tie uncertainty of tens of meters.

features.name: Gediz Vallis
features.subtitle: Ancient channel
features.description: Curiosity examined rock and sediment deposits in the channel. NASA interprets them in the context of ancient floods and debris movement.
features.accuracy: USGS feature center, published to 0.01°. It does not locate any individual rover observation.

features.name: Boxwork formations
features.subtitle: Mount Sharp foothills
features.description: Groundwater deposited minerals in bedrock fractures. Erosion exposed the hardened deposits as a network of low ridges, which Curiosity imaged up close in 2025.
features.accuracy: Individual formation coordinates were not verified.

features.name: Sulfate-bearing unit
features.subtitle: Layered strata
features.description: Curiosity investigated sulfate-bearing layers that help researchers examine the transition toward drier conditions on ancient Mars.
features.accuracy: No georeferenced unit boundary is configured.

features.name: Glen Torridon
features.subtitle: Clay-bearing terrain
features.description: A trough south of Vera Rubin Ridge where Curiosity examined part of the clay-bearing unit.
features.accuracy: No vetted point coordinate is configured.

features.name: Vera Rubin Ridge
features.subtitle: Lower Mount Sharp
features.description: Curiosity studied the ridge before moving into the adjacent clay-bearing terrain at Glen Torridon.
features.accuracy: No vetted point coordinate is configured.

features.name: Perseverance landing
features.subtitle: Mars 2020
features.description: Perseverance touched down in Jezero Crater on February 18, 2021.
features.accuracy: Published NASA landing solution. Coordinate digits are not an uncertainty estimate.
